title: Number of Connected Components In An Undirected Graph
statement: You get n nodes numbered 0 to n-1 and a list of undirected edges. A connected component is a group of nodes that can all reach each other through edges. Return how many components the graph has. A node with no edges is a component by itself.

example.caption: Nodes 0, 1, 2 are linked. 3 and 4 are linked. 5 is alone. That makes 3 components.

idea.sentence: Walk through the nodes. Each time you meet a node no earlier walk reached, start a new walk that marks everything connected to it, and count that start.

jargon.plain: A maximal group of nodes where any one can reach any other by following edges.
For each node, the list of nodes it shares an edge with.
Starting at one node, keep visiting unvisited neighbours until nothing new is reachable.

watch.inputHint: Two arguments: the node count, then the edges, e.g. 6, [[0,1],[1,2],[3,4]]

compare.bruteLabel: Test every pair of nodes for a path

rows.name: Path check for every pair
rows.note: Ask for each pair whether a path exists.

rows.name: DFS flood fill
rows.note: Each node is marked once and each edge is looked at twice. The lists hold every edge.

rows.name: Union-find (alternative)
rows.note: Start with n groups and subtract one for every edge that merges two groups. See Redundant Connection.

fast.takeaway: Marking nodes as you reach them means no node is walked twice. The number of fresh starts equals the number of components.

stages.title: Neighbour lists
stages.note: Store every edge in both directions so each node knows its neighbours.

stages.title: New component
stages.note: At the next node nobody has reached, count a new component and number it.

stages.title: Take a node
stages.note: Pop a node off the stack and look at each of its neighbours.

stages.title: Reach neighbours
stages.note: Mark each unreached neighbour with the current component number and push it.

stages.title: Return the count
stages.note: Every node has a component number. The number of starts is the answer.

edges.title: No edges
edges.why: Each node is its own component. The outer loop starts a walk at every node.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: One node and nothing else is still one component.

edges.title: Duplicate and reversed edges
edges.why: Repeated edges change nothing. The group mark stops a node being pushed twice. Node 2 is alone.

edges.title: One long chain
edges.why: One walk from node 0 reaches everything. The stack replaces recursion, so a long chain cannot overflow.

gotchas.text: Add each undirected edge in both directions. If you only add a to b, a walk that begins at b never gets back to a.
Mark a node when you push it, not when you pop it. Otherwise the same node can sit on the stack many times.
Array(n).fill([]) makes every node share one neighbour list. Use Array.from({ length: n }, () => []). Also todo.pop() is typed number | undefined, so assert it is present after checking the length.
make([][]int, n) gives n nil inner slices. append works on a nil slice, so adj[a] = append(adj[a], b) needs no setup. Popping is todo = todo[:len(todo)-1].

recap.key: Scan nodes. A node not yet reached starts a new component. Flood from it to mark its whole component.
recap.complexity: Time O(n + m). Space O(n + m).
moves: Build neighbour lists in both directions
Scan nodes and start at any unreached one, count it
Pop, and mark and push each unreached neighbour
